verses.restored: When king Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered house of YHWH.
He sent Eliakim over house, Shebna the scribe, and elders of priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.
They said to him, Thus says Hezekiah: This day is day of distress, rebuke, and contempt, for children have come to birth opening, but there is no strength to give birth.

Perhaps YHWH your Divine will hear all words of Rabshakeh, whom king of Assyria his master sent to reproach living Divine, and will rebuke words YHWH your Divine has heard. Lift a prayer for remnant that remains.
Servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, Thus you shall say to your master: Thus says YHWH, Do not fear words you heard, by which young servants of king of Assyria reviled me.
Look, I am putting a spirit in him; he shall hear a report, return to his land, and I will cause him to fall by sword in his own land.
Rabshakeh returned and found king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he heard that he had departed from Lachish.
He heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, Look, he has gone out to fight you. He sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,
Thus you shall say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your Divine in whom you trust deceive you, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into hand of king of Assyria.
Look, you have heard what kings of Assyria did to all lands, devoting them to destruction. Shall you be delivered?
Did gods of nations deliver those my fathers destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and children of Eden in Telassar?
Where is king of Hamath, king of Arpad, and king of city Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?
Hezekiah took letters from hand of messengers and read them. Hezekiah went up to house of YHWH and spread them before YHWH.
Hezekiah prayed before YHWH and said, YHWH, Divine of Israel, sitting above cherubim, you alone are Divine over all kingdoms of earth; you made heavens and earth.
Incline your ear, YHWH, and hear; open your eyes, YHWH, and see. Hear words of Sennacherib, which he sent to reproach living Divine.
Truly, YHWH, kings of Assyria laid waste nations and their lands,
and put their gods into fire, for they were not gods but work of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
Now, YHWH our Divine, please save us from his hand, so all kingdoms of earth may know that you, YHWH, are Divine alone.
Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says YHWH Divine of Israel: What you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard.
This is word YHWH spoke concerning him: Virgin daughter Zion despises you and mocks you; daughter Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you reproached and reviled? Against whom lifted your voice and raised your eyes on high? Against Holy One of Israel.

By your messengers you reproached Lord and said, With multitude of my chariots I ascended height of mountains, farthest parts of Lebanon; I cut down tall cedars and choice cypresses and entered farthest lodging, forest of its fruitful land.
I dug and drank foreign waters, and with soles of my feet dried all streams of besieged places.
Have you not heard? From far ago I made it; from days of old I formed it. Now I brought it to pass, that you should make fortified cities into ruined heaps.
Their inhabitants were short of hand, shattered and ashamed; they became grass of field, green herb, grass of roofs, and scorched grain before standing.
But your sitting, going out, coming in, and raging against me I know.
Because your raging against me and arrogance rose into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and bridle in your lips and turn you back by way you came.
This shall be sign for you: eat this year what grows of itself, second year what springs from it, and in third year sow, reap, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
Surviving remnant of house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For from Jerusalem a remnant shall go out, and survivors from Mount Zion. Zeal of YHWH of hosts shall do this.
Therefore thus says YHWH concerning king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city, shoot an arrow there, come before it with shield, or pour up siege ramp against it.
By way he came, by it he shall return, and to this city he shall not come, says YHWH.
I will shield this city to save it, for my sake and for sake of David my servant.
That night messenger of YHWH went out and struck in camp of Assyria one hundred eighty-five thousand. They rose early in morning, and look, all of them were dead bodies.
Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went, returned, and lived at Nineveh.
As he bowed in house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with sword and escaped to land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.

translation_notes: Hezekiah's torn clothes and sackcloth are crisis rituals, not signs that fear or grief is weak faith.
The birth metaphor describes a community at the point of delivery without strength. It must not shame laboring people, pregnancy complications, infertility, pregnancy loss, or medical intervention.
Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before YHWH; prayer here brings propaganda into honest scrutiny rather than denying military reality.
The prayer polemic calls other gods human-made. It belongs to Israelite monotheistic theology and must not authorize destruction, ridicule, or persecution of living religious communities.
Assyria boasts of deforestation, water control, siege, and ruined cities. Imperial domination includes ecological extraction and destruction.
The hook-in-nose and bridle imagery reflects Assyrian practices of humiliating captives. It is a reversal of imperial violence, not permission for torture.
Agricultural recovery unfolds across three years. Survival after siege includes food systems, planting, time, labor, and land restoration—not an instant return to normal.
Verse 35 reports mass death of 185,000 Assyrians through Divine agency. This is morally dangerous sacred-war material and must not be celebrated, reenacted, or used to pray for mass killing.
Assyrian soldiers are human beings, many under command. Jerusalem's deliverance does not make their corpses spiritually delightful.
Sennacherib is later assassinated by sons in a temple. Patricide and political assassination remain violence; another religion's sanctuary must not be mocked.
Kings/Isaiah/Chronicles and Assyrian sources require historical and source-witness audit regarding the campaign, withdrawal, chronology, and casualty tradition.
safety_note: Do not turn Jerusalem's rescue into joy over 185,000 dead people, justify holy war, mock other religions, or romanticize assassination. Center fear, prayer, remnant survival, agricultural recovery, civilians under siege, conscripted soldiers, and the refusal of empire's claim to be morally unstoppable.
